title: Thames Glide
tagline: Both engines gone at 2,500 ft over east London.
history: Inspired by a 2009 airliner that lost both engines to a flock of geese two minutes after take-off and was ditched, without loss of life, on a river beside a city.
situation: You are climbing out of London City on runway 09 with 98 passengers on a cold, clear afternoon. Passing 2,500 ft over Thamesmead a flock of geese goes through both engines. You have perhaps three minutes of gliding.
failures: Bird strike: both engines destroyed (no relight)
No thrust — battery, APU and RAT only
Glide range from 2,500 ft: about 6 NM
tips: Lower the nose at once: hold about 200 kt clean (best glide)
Turning back to runway 27 costs height you may not have
Ditching: gear up, full flap, wings level, about 11° nose-up, the lowest sink you can

do.note: F/O: Birds! Both engines rolling back — we've lost thrust on both!
ATC: Runway 27 is available, emergency services alerted — say intentions.
F/O: Relight's not working. We may not make a runway — the river is wide open ahead.

objectives.text: Land on a runway or ditch survivably
